newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar firms, deliveries from mills slow.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar firms, deliveries from mills slow.

text.p: Sugar prices in Bombay held a firm tack on Thursday as fresh consumer demand met reduced deliveries from mills to the market, dealers said.
Ready delivery sugar S-30 rose 15 rupees to 1,315/1,350 rupees per quintal while M-30 moved up 10 rupees to 1,375/1,425 rupees.

"Local millers are witnessing higher demand from the bulk consumers as well as from the neighbouring states which in turn curtailed arrivals of sugar from mills to the Bombay market," Shantilal Dedhiya, secretary of Bombay Sugar Merchants' Association, said.
"Higher lifting from the mills also raised prices for sugar mill delivery," he said.
Sugar for mill delivery moved up to 1,255/1,270 rupees from 1,240/1,260.
"Overall sentiment was firm at the close amid shortage of ready stock and market may move up further," Dedhiya added.
